# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (best overall clip-on)**
- Runner's World's top pick, and Wired calls the sound clearer than most rivals. They have physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run.
- The price is $199 (down from $299). Battery lasts about 7 hours per charge and water resistance is IPX4, so they're not ideal for heavy rain.
- Runner's World says Bose has a new pair coming soon, so you may want to wait.
- [Runner's World review with buy links](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (best bone conduction)**
- This is the choice if awareness matters most. It has physical buttons, a 12-hour battery and IP55 rating.
- It lists at $180, but Wired and Runner's World show it around $125-$130 at REI, Best Buy, Walmart and Lowe's.
- Downsides: the neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats, and the bass is only decent.
- [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

**Shokz OpenDots 2 (best for long runs and wet weather)**
- Wired's top pick. It gets 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and has an IP57 rating. Wired's reviewer submerged them without problems.
- It costs $200.
- [WIRED's best open earbuds guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Budget options**
- **Nothing Ear (Open):** SoundGuys' pick for running, with strong bass for the category and an IP54 rating. It was $99 at Amazon (MSRP $149) at the time of the listing. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2:** IP55 and long battery life. SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 at Amazon (see the link above). Dealectric's store shows $129.99, or $104 with code AFSC20 (tested Oct 22), so check Amazon's price first. [Dealectric link](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2). Dealectric earns a commission on that link at no extra cost to you.
- **JLab Flex Open (about $40-$50):** Runner's World calls it the lowest-risk way to try clip-ons. Its sound is thinner. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro ($50):** Wired's cheap pick. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

## Quick guide
- **Best sound and comfort:** Bose
- **Most aware of your surroundings:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2
- **Marathon training or rain:** Shokz OpenDots 2
- **Not sure you'll like open-ear:** JLab or Soundpeats

Open-ear designs sound thinner than sealed earbuds, and none are a safety guarantee. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic. Prices change often, so confirm at checkout.
